{{c|''The Phari{{ls}}ees of Hieru{{ls}}alem comming {{ls}}o farre to carpe him, he chargeth with a tradition contrarie to Gods commaundement. 10 And to the people he yeldeth the rea{{ls}}on of that which they reproued: 15 and againe to his Di{{ls}}ciples, {{ls}}hewing the ground of the Phari{{ls}}aical vva{{ls}}hing (to vvitte, that meates otherwi{{ls}}e defile the {{ls}}oule) to be fal{{ls}}e. 21 then he goeth a{{ls}}ide to hide him {{ls}}elf among the Gentils: where, in a woman he findeth {{ls}}uch faith, that he is faine, le{{ls}}t the Gentils {{ls}}hould before the time extort the whole bread, as {{ls}}he had a crumme, to returne to the Ievves. 34 vvhere (al contrarie to tho{{ls}}e Phari{{ls}}ees) the common people {{ls}}eeke wonderfully vnto him. and he after he hath cured their di{{ls}}ea{{ls}}ed, feedeth 4000 of them with {{ls}}euen loaues.''}}

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō wen{{ls}}day the 3. weeke in Lent.}}{{dropinitial|T|fl={{verse|chapter=15|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Hen}} came to him from Hieru{{ls}}alem Scribes and Phari{{ls}}ees, {{ls}}aying,{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 7, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=2}} VVhy do thy Di{{ls}}ciples tran{{ls}}gre{{ls}}{{ls}}e the tradition of the Auncientes? For they wa{{ls}}h not their hāds when they eate bread. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=3}} But he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid to them: Why do you al{{ls}}o tran{{ls}}gre{{ls}}{{ls}}e the commaundement of God for your tradition? For God {{ls}}aid, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=4}} ''Honour father and mother''. and, ''He that {{ls}}hal cur{{ls}}e father or mother, dying let him dye''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 12.''}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 20, 9.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=5}} But you {{ls}}ay, Who{{ls}}oeuer {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ay to father or mother, The gift vvhat{{ls}}oeuer procedeth from me, {{ls}}hal profite the: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}} and {{ls}}hal not honour his father or his mother: and you haue made fru{{ls}}trate the cōmaundement of God for your ovvne tradition. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}} Hypocrites, vvel hath E{{ls}}ay Prophecied of you, {{ls}}aying, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}} ''This people honoureth me {{sup|‖}} vvith their lippes: but their hart is farre from me''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''E{{ls}}a. 29, 13.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}} ''And in vaine do they vvor{{ls}}hippe me, teaching doctrines and {{sup|‖}} commaundements of men''.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}} And hauing called together the multitudes vnto him, he {{ls}}aid to them, Heare ye and vnder{{ls}}tand. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}} {{sup|‖}} Not that vvhich entreth into the mouth, defileth a man: but that vvhich procedeth out of the mouth, that defileth a man. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}} Then came his Di{{ls}}ciples, and {{ls}}aid to him, Doe{{ls}}t thou knovv that the Phari{{ls}}ees, when they heard this vvord, vvere {{ls}}candalized? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}} But he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}ayd: All planting vvhich my heauenly father hath not planted, {{ls}}hal be rooted vp. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}} Let them alone: blinde they are, guides of the blinde. And if the blinde be guide to the blinde, both fall into the ditch. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}} And Peter an{{ls}}wering {{ls}}ayd to him, Expound vs this parable. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}} But he {{ls}}ayd, Are you al{{ls}}o as yet vvithout vnder{{ls}}tanding? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}} Do you not vnder{{ls}}tand, that al that entreth into the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is ca{{ls}}t forth into the priuy? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}} But the things that proceede out of the mouth, come forth from the hart, and tho{{ls}}e things {{sup|‖}} defile a man. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}} For from the hart come forth euil cogitations, murders, aduoutries, fornications, thefts, fal{{ls}}e te{{ls}}timonies, bla{{ls}}phemies. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}} The{{ls}}e are the things that<noinclude>{{continues|defile}}</noinclude>
